record.title: State-Grounded Conditioning reports lower direction drift in a live game-coaching agent
record.summary: A double-blind preprint introduces State-Grounded Conditioning (SGC), which moves state-dependent tool and response control into three explicit wrappers for intent/context, live fact slots, and session history. On 200 anonymized production sessions (~1,000 turns) from one in-game coaching system, the authors report that Full SGC reached 96.7% turn-level grounded accuracy and 83.5% session-level grounded accuracy, versus 69.8% and 26.5% for their Plan-and-Execute agent baseline; mean first-token latency was 1.5 s versus 6.1 s. Test labels used two independent human annotators with third-annotator adjudication. This is a bounded, author-reported result in one domain. The baseline had less product-specific prompt tuning, some reliability statistics and confidence intervals are deferred to camera-ready, and no transfer outside gaming or direct user outcome is demonstrated.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors propose State-Grounded Conditioning with three wrappers that externalize intent/tool selection, live fact-slot grounding, and cross-turn dialogue control into explicit state-dependent interfaces.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 200 anonymized production sessions sampled over approximately four weeks (~1,000 turns) from one in-game coaching system, Full SGC reports 96.7% turn-level grounded accuracy and 83.5% session-level grounded accuracy, versus 69.8% and 26.5% for PE-Agent; mean first-token latency is 1.5 s versus 6.1 s.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint reports no experimental validation outside the game-coaching deployment, discloses that PE-Agent did not receive the same product-specific prompt tuning as SGC, and defers full agreement estimates, some confidence intervals, and the complete discordant tables to camera-ready supplementary material.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported model-output metrics do not establish improvement in user retention, satisfaction, in-game performance, or other direct user outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported accuracy and latency results have not been independently reproduced or tested in a second product/domain.
The baseline comparison is not effort-matched for product-specific prompt tuning, and full agreement/CI statistics are deferred to camera-ready material.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded result is reproducible, explicit state-dependent wrappers could change architecture choices for live, multi-turn agents in domains with structured state. The evidence is one product domain and does not establish broader transfer.
limitations: Evidence comes from one in-game coaching deployment. Transfer to the three discussed domains is analytical, not experimentally validated.
PE-Agent followed its published specification but did not receive the same iteration of product-specific prompt tuning as SGC; some measured difference may reflect architecture plus tuning.

Full 200-session inter-annotator agreement estimates, some 95% confidence intervals, and complete discordant-pair tables are deferred to camera-ready supplementary material; pilot agreement statistics are reported for a 50-session subset.
The work reports model-output quality and mean first-token latency, not retention, re-engagement, satisfaction, or in-match performance.

Operational applicability requires live user-state constraints, measurable direction-drift cost, and machine-readable state slices; the paper says simpler one-shot or low-stakes tasks may need only a generic harness or retrieval.
brief.summary: A double-blind preprint introduces State-Grounded Conditioning (SGC), which moves state-dependent tool and response control into three explicit wrappers for intent/context, live fact slots, and session history. On 200 anonymized production sessions (~1,000 turns) from one in-game coaching system, the authors report that Full SGC reached 96.7% turn-level grounded accuracy and 83.5% session-level grounded accuracy, versus 69.8% and 26.5% for their Plan-and-Execute agent baseline; mean first-token latency was 1.5 s versus 6.1 s. The baseline had less product-specific prompt tuning, some reliability statistics and confidence intervals are deferred to camera-ready, and no transfer outside gaming or direct user outcome is demonstrated.

technical.claimed_result: Full SGC reports 96.7% turn-level grounded accuracy, 83.5% session-level grounded accuracy, and 1.5 s mean first-token latency on the 200-session benchmark, versus 69.8%, 26.5%, and 6.1 s for PE-Agent. All test metrics are based on dual independent human annotation with adjudication; no LLM-judge labels enter the test metrics.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint defines the method, evaluation protocol, stated deployment regime, and author-reported metrics. The performance and latency measurements remain claims in a single-system paper; the research desk did not reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: SGC decomposes live state into intent/context, factual state slots, and session history. Wrapper W1 selects a tool set and can freeze tool choice early; W2 grounds candidate responses against structured live facts and constraints; W3 schedules cross-turn coaching guidance and writes answer metadata back into session state.
technical.novelty: Separates state-dependent control into explicit wrappers for intent/tool mapping, live factual constraints, and cross-turn guidance, and reports their cumulative results in one deployed agent rather than relying only on generic prompt context or a serial plan-execute pipeline.
technical.regime: One deployed in-game conversational coaching system; 200 anonymized production sessions sampled over about four weeks (~1,000 turns), stratified by evaluation eligibility and session length; five configurations; same serving hardware and network. No empirical transfer to other domains.
technical.reproducibility: The paper reports pre-registered rubrics, hashes for frozen references/rubrics, blinded configuration labels, dual human annotation and third-annotator adjudication. Full artefact and some reliability/CI tables are deferred; no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: PE-Agent shares the same LLM backbone, tool schemas, grounding references, and serving setup, and reports 69.8% turn-level and 26.5% session-level grounding with 6.1 s mean first-token latency. The authors disclose that PE-Agent did not receive the same product-specific prompt tuning during deployment iteration, so the reported gap combines architecture and tuning effects.

brief.title: State-Grounded Conditioning reports lower direction drift in a live game-coaching agent
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported effect holds in similar stateful agents, deterministic wrappers around live intent, facts, and session memory can reduce direction drift while avoiding a serial plan-execute latency path. The result may affect architecture choices for interactive agents where state changes and multi-turn guidance matter; it does not establish general gains across agent domains.
